To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the binding of [3 H]AMPA to rat brain membranes is increased by KSCN, and that this increase is most effective at the low affinity site.

1) [3H]α-AMPA binding to rat brain membranes was increased by Triton X-10, 2) KSCN increased [3H] α-AMPA binding, 3) the rank order of potency for glutamate analogs was quisqualate>AMPA>glutamate>kainate
the binding of [3 H]AMPA to rat brain membranes can be characterized by a filtration assay and that the binding of the ligand is increased by the chaotropic agent KSCN.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pharmacology of [3H]-AMPA binding to rat brain membranes using both centrifugation and a filtration assay technique.
the development of a filtration assay which can be used to quantitatively evaluate quisqualate binding sites.
the identification of the molecular basis for the binding properties of the putative quisqulate receptor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the binding of [3 H]AMPA is a useful tool to characterize quisqualate recognition site(s) in the rat CNS.
the filtration assay is more suitable for studying [3H]glutamate binding sites, while the centrifugation assay is more suitable to study [3H]D-AP5 binding sites.
the binding of [3 H]AMPA to rat brain tissue is a function of the presence of a single receptor site which is modulated by a number of factors, including the chaotropic agent KSCN.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the binding sites for the putative excitatory amino acid receptors are heterogeneous in nature.
the [3H]-AMPA binding site was a high affinity, low capacity site that is sensitive to the chaotrope KSCN.
the binding of [3 H]AMPA is dependent on the presence of a chaotropic agent, potassium thiocyanide, which increases the apparent affinity for the ligand without affecting the number of binding site.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the [3H]-AMPA assay is not a good assay for the quisqualate receptor.
we have shown that the use of a chaotropic agent can be used to enhance the binding of [3 H]AMPA to its receptor.
the binding sites of the three ligands, quisqualate, kainic acid and AMPA are not identical.
